evals.prompt: Write a 5-step cold email sequence to Heads of IT at 200–1,000 employee healthcare companies for our identity management product.
evals.expected_output: Researched hooks, short emails, new angle per step, lowercase subjects, soft CTAs.
assertions: Each follow-up adds a new angle

evals.prompt: We're sending cold email from our main domain and landing in spam.
evals.expected_output: Infrastructure fixes: secondary domains, auth, warmup, volume limits.

evals.prompt: A prospect replied: 'Interesting, but we're locked into a contract with our current vendor until June.' What do we do?
evals.expected_output: Classifies as timing, stops the sequence on every channel, drafts a short reply, sets a dated follow-up before June, logs it.
assertions: Classifies the reply as timing / not now
Stops all automated steps for this contact
Sets a dated follow-up ahead of the renewal
Logs the outcome in the CRM

evals.prompt: Review this cold email: 'Hi Sam, I hope this finds you well! My name is Alex and I'm with Acme. We offer AI dashboards, automated alerts, 40+ integrations, and SOC 2 compliance. Do you have 30 minutes this week for a call?'
evals.expected_output: Redline that removes the self-intro and pleasantry, replaces the feature list with one proof point, swaps the meeting ask for an interest question, and adds relevant personalization.
assertions: Flags the self-introduction and stock pleasantry
Cuts the feature list to one proof point
Replaces the 30-minute ask with a low-friction question
Uses no AI-isms from the Don'ts list
